canonical_title: Cathedral researchers accessed limited Anthropic internal systems through third-party business software
aliases: Cathedral Anthropic third party SaaS breach
Washington Post Anthropic Cathedral security incident
products: Anthropic internal sales HR IT systems
treatment: Treat as security disclosure distinct from Claude autonomous-agent unauthorized actions; reinclude only for independently corroborated technical details, confirmed expanded data impact, vendor CVEs, mitigations or regulatory action.
known_facts: Washington Post exclusive published 2026-10-26 01:00 EDT = 14:00 JST reports Cathedral security researchers accessed limited Anthropic internal sales, HR and IT data through vulnerabilities in third-party business software under a security testing program.
The report says researchers used AI agents for under 12 hours after earlier attempts; Anthropic confirmed access to a limited set of systems and reported some activity was detected by its monitoring.
Anthropic stated Claude customer conversations, generated responses, source code and model weights were not accessed; no evidence of exploitation beyond Cathedral was found.

Anthropic disabled the affected business software and restored it only after vendor remediation; Anthropic disputed Cathedral's national security framing and alleged incomplete disclosure of researcher activity.
reinclude_only_if: Affected vendor names, CVEs, exploit prerequisites, or reproducible technical root cause are published.
Anthropic or regulators confirm broader customer impact, further exploitation or new containment measures.
Independent incident report resolves disagreements over authorization and scope.
notes: NEW independent reporting in night window; researcher findings and Anthropic statement have different scopes, do not claim model weights compromised.
